items.headline: Results are appended one row per training run, with a header written only when the file does not yet exist, so a killed job still leaves a valid partial CSV.
items.verbatim:
def save_results(filepath, s, iteration, model, rep, n, metrics, params_source='default', loss_function='mse'):
    """
    Save results to a CSV file with loss function tracking
    """
    if filepath:
        file_exists = os.path.isfile(filepath)

        with open(filepath, mode='a', newline='') as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            
            # Write header if the file is new
            if not file_exists:
                writer.writerow(["sigma", "iteration", "model", "rep", "sample_size", "mae", "mse", "rmse", "r2", "pearson_corr", "params_source", "loss_function"])
            
            # Save the results
            writer.writerow([s, iteration, model, rep, n, metrics[0], metrics[1], metrics[2], metrics[3], metrics[4], params_source, loss_function])
items.verification: verified — read in full
items.why_it_matters: Twelve columns, in this order. A complete job writes 11 noise levels times 10 replicates = 110 data rows. Because rows are appended as they are produced, the zero-noise rows of a job that is still running are already on disk and readable now.

items.why_it_matters: This is the decisive line for question 3. At noise level zero the strategy label is inert, so the redesign of the noise scheme cannot invalidate those rows. It also means the six strategy files hold six replays of the same experiment, not six different conditions.

items.headline: The random seed is fixed at 42 and is not overridden by any of the 24 scripts, so the six strategy files replay the same ten clean runs rather than giving thirty extra replicates.

items.headline: A second, independent confound above zero: the standardisation statistics are computed from the already-noised training labels.
items.verification: verified — the mean and standard deviation are then taken from y_values at /Users/apunt/repos/qsar_qm_models/rust/src/main.rs:973-978 and applied at :760
items.why_it_matters: Even if the held-out defect were absent, the above-zero rows would still be standardised by a noise-inflated spread. At noise level zero the map is empty, so the statistics come from clean labels and this confound is absent too.

items.headline: The lowercase kernel flag does map to the RBF kernel and to the gauche_rbf label, so the rows will be labelled correctly.
items.verification: verified — the label is then set at /Users/apunt/repos/qsar_qm_models/models/models.py:1787 as: model_name = 'gauche_rbf' if params['kernel_name'] == 'RBF' else 'gauche'
items.why_it_matters: I checked this because the scripts pass --kernel rbf in lowercase while the label test compares against uppercase RBF. The capitalise-then-special-case path saves it. The tuned-hyperparameter branch that would have silently overridden the kernel is gated on --use-best-params (/Users/apunt/repos/qsar_qm_models/scripts/process_and_train.py:265, store_true, default off) and no gauche_rbf script passes it, so params_source should read default on every row. cd /data/stat-cadd/scat9264/qsar_qm_models/results

items.headline: Step 8 — the analysis that answers the kernel question, on the zero-noise rows only.
items.verbatim:
import glob, re, pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import wilcoxon
D = '/Users/apunt/repos/qsar_qm_models/results/gp_kernel_harvest/qm9/'
r = []
for f in glob.glob(D + 'anova_*_gauche*.csv'):
    d = pd.read_csv(f)
    d = d[d.sigma.astype(float) == 0.0].copy()
    d['strat'] = re.search(r'anova_([a-z]+)_', f).group(1)
    r.append(d)
a = pd.concat(r, ignore_index=True)
g = a.groupby(['model', 'rep', 'iteration']).r2.agg(['nunique', 'count'])
print('replays that DISAGREE at sigma=0 (should be empty):')
print(g[g['nunique'] > 1])
b = a.drop_duplicates(['model', 'rep', 'iteration'])
p = b.pivot_table(index=['rep', 'iteration'], columns='model',
                  values='r2').dropna()
for rep, x in p.groupby(level=0):
    d = x.gauche_rbf - x.gauche
    print(rep, 'n=%d' % len(x), 'median(RBF-Tanimoto)=%+.4f' % d.median(),
          wilcoxon(x.gauche_rbf, x.gauche))

At that level no noise is drawn, the strategy label is inert, the held-out-label defect cannot fire because there is nothing to apply, and the standardisation statistics come from clean labels. DOES NOT SURVIVE — every row at sigma 0.1 through 1.0. On QM9 those carry the held-out-label defect from the pre-fix binary and the noise-inflated standardisation. On both studies they are additionally on the superseded axis: the redesign replaces the single knob with a realised dose and replaces the strategy set, so nothing measured against the old sigma is comparable to what comes next. One further caution: the binary is loaded fresh by each subprocess call, so if it was rebuilt while a job was running that job's file can mix pre-fix and post-fix rows above zero. The zero rows are unaffected either way.
